name: Russia–NATO
value: Drone in Polish airspace 23 Nov; no Article 4
summary: Russian drone briefly entered Polish airspace on 23 Nov; NATO sending surveillance aircraft to Poland
state: A Russian drone briefly violated Polish airspace on 23 Nov during a strike on western Ukraine and was not shot down (Kiprinform), and NATO said on 24 Nov it would send surveillance aircraft to Poland after Russian missile strikes near the border (Notes from Poland). An IISS study reported on 27 Nov that Russian sabotage attacks in Europe rose 16% (NBC News). No Article 4 request or direct clash was found to 28 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Airspace incidents on NATO's eastern flank can disrupt flights near the Polish and Baltic borders. Travellers should follow FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Drone airspace violation on NATO territory = Watch; no Article 4 or clash

why: Direct Russia–NATO confrontation is the most likely path to a European war involving the UK.
drivers: Airspace and drone incursions, sabotage, Baltic incidents, nuclear signalling, Ukraine war spillover.

rubric.alert: Article 4 consultations, a direct military clash, or an attack on NATO territory.
rubric.watch: Airspace/drone violations, sabotage attributed to Russia, or explicit threats against members.
rubric.normal: No notable incidents on NATO territory in the past two weeks.
